items.title: Where the filter is
items.caption: The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.
items.alt: Diagram: dishwasher floor with the cylindrical filter that twists out to rinse
items.relatedCheck: clean the drain filter

items.title: dishwasher not cleaning properly not draining
Check and rinse the spray arm
items.caption: The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.
items.alt: Diagram: dishwasher spray arm with jet holes and a spin-check arrow
items.relatedCheck: clear the spray-arm jets and check the arms spin

items.title: Fridge not cooling — simple checks first
items.caption: Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.
items.alt: Infographic: fridge-freezer showing the temperature setting, door seal, rear condenser coils and ventilation gap to check
items.relatedCheck: check the temperature setting, door seal and ventilation, and clean the condenser coils

items.title: About the hob heating parts
items.caption: When a hob zone won't heat or heats unevenly, the parts involved are the heating element/zone, the temperature sensor and the control board — and on an induction hob, the pan itself must be suitable. This reference shows where they sit and the safe checks (use the right pan, keep the surface clean, try a reset). Replacing hob parts is a job for a qualified engineer.
items.alt: Reference diagram: a hob with its heating zones, temperature sensor, control board and power connection labelled, alongside customer-safe checks
items.relatedCheck: identify the hob heating parts and the safe pre-checks for a zone that will not heat or heats unevenly

items.title: oven cooker not heating cooking properly
About uneven oven heating
items.caption: When an oven cooks unevenly or browns on one side, the parts usually involved are the fan that circulates the heat, the element, the temperature sensor and the door seal. This reference shows where they sit and the safe checks worth making. Replacing these parts is a job for a qualified engineer.
items.alt: Reference diagram: an oven showing the parts involved in even heating — fan, element, temperature sensor and door seal — with customer-safe checks
items.relatedCheck: identify the parts behind uneven oven heating and the safe pre-checks

items.title: Where the condenser and water tank are
items.caption: On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.
items.alt: Diagram: condenser dryer with the pull-out water tank on top and the condenser behind a lower flap
items.relatedCheck: clear the condensate path / clean the condenser

items.title: Where the lint filter is
items.caption: The fluff/lint filter sits in the door opening or just inside the rim. Lift it out and clear the fluff after every load. Typical layout — your dryer may differ.
items.alt: Diagram: tumble-dryer door open with the lint filter in the door opening
items.relatedCheck: clean the lint/fluff filter

items.title: Tumble dryer not drying properly — what to check
items.caption: Poor drying is most often caused by restricted airflow. Clean the fluff filter every cycle, clean the condenser regularly and avoid overloading the drum — these are safe checks you can do yourself. Switch the dryer off and let it cool first.
items.alt: Reference diagram: a tumble dryer's airflow path highlighting the fluff filter and condenser to clean for better drying
items.relatedCheck: clean the fluff filter and condenser and avoid overloading to restore drying performance

items.title: Tumble dryer runs but doesn't heat — what to check
items.caption: If the drum turns but the clothes stay wet, it's usually a heating fault — and the most common cause is restricted airflow, which you can fix yourself. Clean the fluff filter and the condenser and clear the vents/ducts. Switch the dryer off and let it cool first.
items.alt: Reference diagram: a tumble dryer's heater element, thermostat, sensor and control board, with customer-safe checks — clean the fluff filter, clean the condenser, clear the vents
items.relatedCheck: clean the fluff filter and condenser and clear the vents to restore airflow before suspecting a heating part

items.title: Poor suction — what to check first
items.caption: Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.
items.alt: Infographic: cylinder vacuum showing the dust container, filters, hose, telescopic tube and floor head to check for blockages
items.relatedCheck: empty the bin, clean the filters and clear any blockage

items.title: Dirty water backing up — check the household waste plumbing
items.caption: If the machine pumps out but dirty water comes back into the drum, backs up the sink, or smells of drains, the problem is usually the HOUSEHOLD WASTE PLUMBING — a blocked standpipe, waste trap/U-bend, or the kitchen sink waste the drain hose feeds into — not the machine's own pump or filter. Check and clear the standpipe and waste connection. Typical layout — your installation may differ.
items.alt: Infographic: washing-machine drain hose feeding a sink waste / standpipe, showing where a blocked household waste trap makes dirty water back up into the machine
items.relatedCheck: check and clear the standpipe / household waste plumbing the drain hose empties into

items.title: Clean the detergent drawer
items.caption: Detergent and softener residue builds up in the drawer and can go mouldy. Pull the drawer right out and rinse it. Typical layout — your machine may differ.
items.alt: Diagram: pull-out detergent drawer with pre-wash, main and softener compartments
items.relatedCheck: clean the drawer

items.title: About the door lock (interlock)
items.caption: The door lock (interlock) keeps the door shut during a wash and stops the machine starting unless the door is locked. This reference shows where it sits. If the door won't open, wait 2–3 minutes after the cycle ends for the lock to release before trying again. A faulty interlock is a replacement part best fitted by a qualified engineer.
items.alt: Reference diagram: a washing machine door lock (interlock) located in the door frame, with a typical interlock component shown
items.relatedCheck: identify the door lock (interlock) and the safe wait-to-release step before the door will open

items.title: Wipe the door-seal fold
items.caption: The rubber door seal has a fold at the bottom where water and gunge collect and go mouldy. Peel it back gently and wipe it clean. Typical layout — your machine may differ.
items.alt: Diagram: washing-machine door boot seal with the lower fold where gunge collects
items.relatedCheck: wipe the door-seal folds

items.title: Where the fill-hose mesh filter is
items.caption: A small mesh filter sits inside the fill-hose connector at the tap/valve end and catches grit. Turn the tap off, unscrew the hose and rinse the mesh. Typical layout — your machine may differ.
items.alt: Diagram: cold tap, fill hose and the mesh filter inside the hose connector
items.relatedCheck: check the fill hose and its inlet mesh filter

items.title: Where the pump filter is
items.caption: The pump filter is usually behind a flap at the bottom front. Turn the machine off and drain any water first, then twist the filter out to clear it. Typical location — your machine may differ.
items.alt: Diagram: front of a washing machine with the pump-filter access flap at the bottom front
items.relatedCheck: inspect and clean the accessible pump filter

items.title: Check the transit bolts have been removed
items.caption: Transit bolts hold the drum still for delivery and must be removed before use — a machine that bangs, walks or vibrates (especially when new or recently moved) often still has them fitted. They unscrew from the back of the machine. Typical layout — your machine may differ.
items.alt: Infographic: rear of a washing machine showing the transit bolts to unscrew, and correct versus incorrect drum movement
items.relatedCheck: check the transit bolts have been removed and the machine is level

items.title: How to unblock the pump / drain filter
items.caption: Typical procedure for clearing a blocked pump filter and drain pump — switch the machine off and drain the water first. Access can vary by model.
items.relatedCheck: inspect and clean the accessible pump filter

items.title: Hotpoint & Indesit won't drain (F05 / F11) — DIY fix
items.caption: Clearing the pump and filter on Hotpoint/Indesit machines that won't drain and show F05 or F11 — switch off and drain the water first. Access can vary by model.
items.relatedCheck: inspect and clean the accessible pump filter

items.title: LG won't drain (OE error) — what to check
items.caption: The common reasons an LG washer shows OE and won't drain, starting with the drain pump filter — switch off and drain the water first. Access can vary by model.
items.relatedCheck: inspect and clean the accessible pump filter

items.title: Clean the seal & drum to remove mould and smells
items.caption: Clearing mould and musty smells by cleaning the door-seal folds and drum and running a hot maintenance wash. For a musty/mouldy smell — not a drain/sewer smell.
items.relatedCheck: wipe the door-seal folds and run a hot maintenance wash
